records.reason: Measure pyridyl ketone m66 at 2/1 with the same loading conditions as its measured 5/1 row, 49201b5817f204116f7f. That acquisition underestimated V2 by 98.62 mL. The current 16.37/43.94-mL prediction tests whether retraining has learned the solvent transition surrounding this major failure.

m90 at 2/1 holds loading fixed relative to its measured 5/1 window of 30.71/60.60 mL in 855832bd4005ac7abdc6. Together with selected m66 at 2/1, it tests ketone-versus-ester transfer under closely matched pyridyl-compound conditions.

m90 at 10/1 completes a fixed-loading solvent bracket around measured 5/1 and selected 2/1. Its predicted 36.07/71.95-mL window implies a smaller additional change beyond 5/1; measurement tests that response shape after the historical 40.19-mL V2 underestimate.

Meta-aminobenzoate m88 at 2/1 keeps the loading variables of d2921349ba8d9cef15a4, whose measured 5/1 window was 26.69/61.83 mL. The current 9.34/16.63-mL prediction places a substantial transition between these ratios, providing a direct test of aminoaryl solvent sensitivity.

Para-aminoacetophenone m36 at 1/1 retains the sample loading and 900-ul DCM plug of 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7. Its predicted 7.10/16.99-mL window contrasts with the measured 2/1 window of 22.32/39.86 mL, testing whether the model locates this strong response at the correct solvent strength.

Para-aminobenzoate m86 at 5/1 follows measured 2/1 row d7f5057912ffbf1231a3 at identical loading. The 33.72/70.82-mL prediction tests whether the large response learned from meta isomer m88 transfers to the para isomer. Cross-isomer comparisons retain their different loading conditions explicitly.

Methyl-substituted quinoline m146 at 5/1 holds loading fixed relative to 9e3ce3497298084abd83, measured at 59.58/106.50 mL at 10/1. The predicted 30.35/50.66-mL window tests the inferred response below a condition with a historical V2 error of -52.02 mL.

2,6-Dimethylpyridine m141 at 10/1 retains the 150-ul loading of measured 1/1 row de4e10d3a5d448ffcdda. Its predicted 21.07/40.71-mL window tests transfer to a sterically flanked basic nitrogen. Reduced silica accessibility is a chemical hypothesis, not an established explanation of its retention.

Quinoline m216 at 5/1 provides a fixed-loading contrast with measured 10/1 row e47aebe2660b9e1528de, 53.42/92.93 mL. Alongside the m146 follow-up, it tests whether related fused nitrogen heteroaromatics share a transition or require distinct condition-response relationships.

Naphthylethanol m205 at 2/1 retains the loading of 48853fd78c77153b963a, whose measured 5/1 window was 51.43/98.38 mL. The current prediction drops to 16.54/35.30 mL. This tests the stronger-solvent response after a 67.34-mL historical V2 underestimate.

Naphthylmethanol m206 at 1/1 holds loading fixed relative to 614873124b33029a924c, measured at 26.06/57.81 mL at 5/1. Its predicted 9.52/26.21-mL window extends learning beyond fitting the single retained-alcohol label and constrains onset and completion separately.

Unobserved methoxyphenylethanol m119 at 5/1 tests transfer from the recently underestimated primary alcohols m205 and m206 to an aromatic alcohol with an additional ether. The predicted 25.88/47.71-mL window is unverified; its paired 1/1 experiment supplies an interpretable solvent contrast.

m119 at 1/1 uses exactly the recorded loading conditions of the selected 5/1 experiment. Its predicted 10.43/16.14-mL window establishes the stronger-solvent endpoint of a new-molecule response curve, distinguishing a general retention offset from an incorrectly transferred solvent sensitivity.

Cinnamic acid m173 at 1/1 changes the DCM plug from the measured 2000 ul to 1500 ul at nearly identical sample amount. Row f90a5a5a54509c085ebd finished at 108.89 mL, versus 45.06 mL at measured 2/1. This tests persistence of the unusual completion result without assuming its cause.

m173 at 5/1 shares the selected 1/1 sample loading and 1500-ul DCM plug. Measured 5/1 row 1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8 used 2000 ul and finished at 60.92 mL. The pair tests whether the isolated 1/1 completion maximum persists across plug volumes and prevents its automatic propagation through the solvent curve.

m81 at 5/1, 50 ul begins a loading contrast at a weaker solvent than the completed 1/1 and 2/1 comparisons. Low-loading measurements fa5d86f56c1c38fa9416 and 36c9891cc52de490659d finished later than their higher-loading counterparts. This tests whether that pattern extends to another ratio.

m81 at 5/1, 150 ul completes the selected loading contrast with all other recorded conditions fixed. The two predictions are almost identical, approximately 7.24/16.02 mL, despite substantial measured loading-associated V2 differences at 1/1 and 2/1 in 06c0c99f1cfb752ed34b and bee82d193ec1ce4fde27.

m32 at 2/1, 100 ul fills the intermediate loading between d73810c9779aede1ff57 and 05a6276f67b3cca8cc7f, whose V2 values were 8.24 and 15.79 mL. It tests whether the high-loading completion excursion belongs to a continuous relationship or is isolated; the existing 1/1 loading comparison has a different pattern.

m25 at 10/1, 150 ul directly contrasts with measured 50-ul row 61e2b18d9ec61505948c. At 2/1, rows 020187ef7e68c736fde7 and ac6cfe67adcb860efabf showed substantially earlier endpoints at higher loading. This tests persistence versus solvent dependence of that loading-associated difference.

New dibenzyl ether m213 at 10/1 is paired with dibenzylamine m212 at the same sample volume, loading solvent and plug volume. Its compact 7.54/13.47-mL prediction tests the structural distinction between ether and secondary amine environments, while their recorded densities remain separate loading covariates.

m212 at 10/1 retains the 150-ul loading of measured 5/1 row 89d752b5a7f7c8d0b91e, 23.21/39.84 mL. It extends basic-nitrogen learning to a secondary benzylamine and anchors the selected ether comparison. The predicted 41.83/65.10-mL response remains untested.

New meta-fluoropropiophenone m65 supplies a compact carbocyclic aryl-ketone control at 5/1, predicted 7.04/14.03 mL. Its sample volume, loading solvent and plug match pyridyl ketone measurement 49201b5817f204116f7f, with a different recorded density. It tests how specifically the severe pyridyl failure transfers across ring environments.

New methyl-substituted tetralone m63 probes substitution and ring-conformation transfer in cyclic aryl ketones. Its predicted 50/1 window, 15.07/30.71 mL, is markedly earlier than the unmeasured tetralone m180 prediction at that ratio. Measured m180 row 983a604ac43bb4d41238 provides only a stronger-solvent structural reference.

New acetylfluorene m38 at 10/1 tests transfer between an external acetyl group on a fused ring system and ring-incorporated carbonyls. Measured naphthyl ketone 1a382a7d3a13ed7fb28f and fluorenone c9e08e156472783dee4e are structural references with different loading conditions; the 1000-ul DCM plug remains an explicit covariate.

New chalcone m165 adds a conjugated diaryl ketone between measured dibenzylideneacetone m164 and unconjugated diaryl ketone m171, represented by b7fffd840d208b29776c and 3c358af26c2e2988cd46 at other ratios. Its modest 10/1 prediction tests transfer of conjugation and carbonyl environment rather than assuming aromatic size determines retention.

New hydroxy-methoxybenzaldehyde m117 at 5/1 tests an ortho OH/carbonyl environment with an additional ether. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding could modify silica interactions, but is an untested prior. Measured salicylaldehyde d227db4f4b8fdca822d5 and fused ether-aldehyde 39815ababe97d7acc107 provide related, differently loaded references.

New ortho-chloroiodobenzene m151 samples a sparsely covered mixed-halogen arrangement at 50/1 despite a compact 6.14/11.25-mL prediction. Previous halogen references such as 7d4077da333ed637ab36 and 8f84fa7c65453783c74e had modest historical errors. One structurally distant label tests whether that successful transfer extends to this gap.

Terephthalaldehyde m191 at 10/1 keeps the loading of measured 2/1 row acdffd73c7b1388ba321, 7.20/21.00 mL. The predicted 18.71/55.61-mL window tests differential growth of onset and completion in a two-carbonyl structure, complementing the modest-onset, longer-completion result for m178 in 634f21e11a8442494ce3.

New para-bromoacetophenone m30 at 50/1 is paired with its ortho isomer to test positional transfer within the densely represented aryl-ketone family. The predicted 16.64/33.88-mL window is similar to the ortho prediction; measurement determines whether that apparent equivalence is justified. Sample mass differs because the recorded densities differ.

New ortho-bromoacetophenone m43 matches the selected para isomer in PE/EA, sample volume, DCM loading solvent and plug volume. The pair tests whether ortho substitution changes the carbonyl response beyond the model's similar predictions. Recorded sample amounts, 147.6 versus 164 mg, remain explicit covariates.

Thioether aldehyde m129 at 20/1 retains the loading of cf8ab33c25ad391a584c, whose measured 5/1 window was only 6.10/17.18 mL despite a much later acquisition prediction. The current 20.13/44.25-mL prediction tests whether a delayed regime emerges at weaker solvent or the earlier overprediction persists around the molecule.

Rigid acrylate m23 at 1/1 has predicted V1/V2 of 4.61/3.60 mL, placing completion before onset. Existing m23 measurements 754baa7688e8c45c8ea8 and 8aeb3c33c4cded8425b9 cover PE-rich conditions at lower loading. This label targets a joint-endpoint failure in the uncovered EA-richer regime and may improve transfer among compact ester rows.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environments require distinct structure-condition relationships. Recent pyridyl, aminoaryl, tertiary-amino and quinoline acquisitions exposed substantial retention underestimates, including failures hidden behind compact predictions. Basicity and nitrogen accessibility are plausible explanatory priors, but the measured failures do not establish one universal nitrogen correction or solvent-response curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: One newly measured condition per molecule can repair a local prediction while leaving the surrounding response curve wrong. Matched solvent contrasts and carbocyclic/ether controls can teach transferable distinctions among nitrogen environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the pyridyl, aminoaryl and fused nitrogen compounds transition into delayed elution, and does transfer to sterically flanked pyridine and secondary benzylamine remain accurate?

hypotheses.content: The primary aromatic-alcohol failures depend on structural environment and solvent strength; an OH count alone is insufficient. Naphthylethanol and naphthylmethanol were substantially underestimated, while the secondary-alcohol acquisition was accurate and the substituted phenol was overpredicted. Transfer to methoxy-substituted primary alcohols remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Solvent contrasts around the failed alcohols distinguish a molecule-specific offset from a misplaced response transition. A new methoxyphenylethanol curve tests whether corrections generalize beyond the acquired structures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the naphthyl alcohols become compact at stronger solvent as predicted, and does the added ether in m119 change the onset and completion responses in a transferable way?

hypotheses.content: Delayed onset and prolonged completion require separate relationships. Feedback includes a very large completion error with modest onset error, underestimated completion in a multifunctional ketone, and false predictions of late or broad elution. Neither a polarity prior nor a broad single-predictor quantile span is sufficient evidence of a long measured elution interval.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels spanning compact, delayed and extended-completion regimes can correct opposing endpoint failures without uniformly increasing predicted retention. The m23 ordering failure also exposes an inaccurate joint mapping of V1 and V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can the model predict completion independently of onset for the acid and dialdehyde follow-ups while preserving sensible endpoint ordering in compact ester conditions?

hypotheses.content: Loading-associated differences are molecule- and possibly ratio-dependent, with their mechanism unresolved. Higher loading coincided with earlier completion for m81 at both measured ratios and earlier endpoints for m25 at 2/1. m32 instead showed much later completion at higher loading at 2/1. These contrasts challenge the predictor's near-invariance but do not establish a universal saturation effect.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Additional controlled contrasts can reveal whether density-times-volume loading needs interactions with structure and PE/EA, while intermediate loading helps distinguish a coherent response from an isolated endpoint excursion.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m81 retain earlier completion at higher loading at 5/1, does m25 retain that direction at 10/1, and does intermediate m32 loading connect its two 2/1 completion values?

hypotheses.content: PE/EA response is molecule-specific, and response anomalies need measurement rather than a universal monotonic rule. The m17 pair disproved the predictor's earlier reversal: both measured endpoints increased from 1/1 to 5/1. Conversely, cinnamic acid has an isolated recorded V2 maximum at 1/1, while m14 was nearly flat between 10/1 and 50/1. The acid maximum's persistence and cause remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local solvent experiments distinguish real transitions, flat regions and unsupported response shapes. They prevent an isolated extreme label or an incorrect chemical prior from imposing the same curve on neighboring rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does cinnamic acid retain the 1/1 completion maximum with a 1500-ul plug, and does m129 actually enter delayed elution at 20/1 after its compact measured 5/1 result?

hypotheses.content: Identical recorded molecule-condition tuples can have appreciably different labels in this catalog. Their source is unknown, so individual surprising endpoints cannot all be assigned confidently to solvent or loading mechanisms. Adjacent-condition comparisons should be interpreted as evidence about recorded relationships, with this variability retained as a limitation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This limits causal interpretation of isolated excursions and favors coherent local comparisons before fitting a strong loading or solvent mechanism. It also cautions against treating quantile spans as purely reducible model uncertainty.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the added intermediate-loading and neighboring-ratio labels form consistent local patterns, or do large endpoint excursions remain isolated?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback substantially strengthened the nitrogen failure hypothesis: m66, m90, m88, m36, m19 and m146 all eluted later than their acquisition predictions. The m66 V2 error was -98.62 mL, and compact predictions failed for m19 as well. Current predictions have incorporated these labels, so the next question is whether their surrounding solvent curves are correct, not whether the historical errors remain current residuals. Alcohol feedback likewise revealed strong structural differences: m205 and m206 were underestimated, whereas m60 was accurate and m58 was overpredicted. The cinnamic-acid 1/1 result, 6.51/108.89 mL, supports learning completion separately from onset but weakens any smooth response interpretation without local confirmation. Its completion exceeds the measured pure-EA, 2/1 and 5/1 values. Conversely, m11 at 10/1 and m129 at 5/1 confirmed substantial overprediction, arguing against a global increase in retention. The m17 measurements rejected the predicted reversal; the original concern is resolved for that pair and carried forward as a response-shape lesson. Completed loading comparisons now show earlier high-loading completion for m81 at both ratios and earlier high-loading endpoints for m25 at 2/1, but the opposite completion direction for m32 at 2/1. This motivates targeted interaction tests rather than a universal loading effect. Finally, m124's unusual delayed pure-EA interval did not persist at doubled loading, which returned 4.21/9.90 mL; that outcome leaves loading versus isolated variability unresolved and reduces the value of broadly propagating its earlier anomaly.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with tests of whether that repair transfers across conditions and structures. Nitrogen follow-ups bracket severe historical failures at fixed loading, while quinoline, lutidine, secondary amine, ether and carbocyclic ketone labels distinguish different nitrogen environments from generic polarity transfer. Alcohol follow-ups test stronger-solvent behavior, and the paired new m119 experiments separate a structural offset from an incorrect solvent sensitivity. The two acid experiments form a matched solvent comparison at a new plug volume and connect to measured counterparts, addressing the unusual completion maximum without assuming a mechanism. Loading experiments extend existing contrasts and fill an intermediate point where the measured direction is inconsistent across families. Exploration is directed toward reusable gaps: ring substitution and carbonyl placement, conjugation, ortho donor/carbonyl environments, halogen position and mixed-halogen structure. Compact predictions for the ether, fluoroketone and mixed-halogen compound, plus m23's reversed endpoint order, counterbalance the delayed-elution experiments. The m129 and dialdehyde measurements test opposing completion-response concerns. These labels may improve interpolation and structural transfer across the Row-distribution while avoiding redundant acquisitions of identical recorded tuples. Loading and plug differences remain explicit covariates, and known recorded-condition variability limits mechanistic conclusions from individual outcomes.
